subject: Re: Urgent: sustained p95/p99 latency regressions affecting Stellarnet pipeline

Subject: Urgent: sustained p95/p99 latency spikes since 02/18

Marissa / Redwood support,

We started seeing severe latency regressions yesterday (02/18) across our production calls to the Hosted API. Our telemetry shows p95s jumping to ~2.1s (normally ~300–400ms) and p99s spiking to 8–12s with occasional 504s. Throughput is steady, but requests are backing up in the queue and we see elevated error rates as the system times out downstream. This is impacting our chat flows and user conversion.

Attached is a screenshot of our dashboard for the past 24 hours and a few request IDs: rreq_7a1f, rreq_7b2c. Can you confirm root cause and ETA for a fix? We are on a time-sensitive launch and this is blocking traffic.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez

Marta.Lopez@stellarnet.com

Subject: [Internal] P0: Stellarnet experiencing p95/p99 regressions — possible queue backlog

Dylan / Rishi — FYI, Stellarnet (DL-4821) reporting p95 ~2.1s and p99 8–12s; customer seeing timeouts and elevated 504s. Attached screenshot and two request IDs. Neha, I'm looping you for CS coordination.

Observed from customer: throughput unchanged, but requests are building in theservice queue and tail latency is ballooning. Hypothesis from initial checks: recent queue/batching policy change may be allowing too many inflight requests (increased max_queue_depth / batching window), causing head-of-line blocking when a small number of long-running requests hit the worker and push others to wait.

Impact: high — affecting core chat UX; customer is asking for ETA and credits.

Ask:
- Dylan: Can you confirm whether any batching/queue_depth changes were deployed on 02/18–02/19 (config, hotfix, or deploy)?
- Rishi / Neha: Please prepare a concise customer-facing status and mitigate churn risk (offer temporary rate-limits or traffic reroute to alternative model if needed).

I'll open an incident and escalate if engineering confirms a config regression.

—Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-19T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [Internal] P0: Stellarnet experiencing p95/p99 regressions — possible queue backlog

Marissa — quick update from infra triage.

What we found (prelim):
- On 2026-02-18 03:14 UTC a rolling config change adjusted the batching dispatcher defaults to increase max_inflight_per_worker from 8 -> 16 and the queue depth ceiling to allow longer batching windows. The change aims to improve throughput, but under mixed request-size workloads it can increase head-of-line blocking.
- Our traces show a small fraction (~0.7%) of requests with long model decode times that hold the worker for multiple seconds; with higher concurrency these long requests cause the queue to back up and p95/p99 to climb. This matches customer telemetry.
- No code regressions; config-only.

Immediate mitigations applied (12:00 PST):
1) Reverted the dispatcher concurrency bump on the affected host pool (rollback rollout started).
2) Reduced default batching window from 40ms -> 20ms for the Hosted API tier to favor latency over throughput while we investigate.
3) Enabled speculative dispatch for requests that exceed 800ms in-queue.

Observations: after the partial rollback we see p95 improve by ~35% in sampled regions, and error rates drop. We are pushing the remaining rollback across remaining pools (ETA 45 min).

Next steps:
- Complete rollback + run targeted canary for 30m.
- Create postmortem and a permanent policy: smarter queue_depth auto-tuning based on tail latency. Logged Jira: TKT-8342.

I'll update this thread when the full rollback completes and include graphs.

—Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook snippet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-20T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Exec summary & ask: Stellarnet P0 (DL-4821) — p95/p99 regressions linked to batching/queue config change

Grace / Neha / Rishi — quick executive update and ask for approval. Full timeline and attachments are included.

Summary:
- Customer: Stellarnet (DL-4821) reported p95 ~2.1s, p99 8–12s beginning 2026-02-18.
- Root cause (prelim): a config-only change on 2026-02-18 increased dispatcher concurrency and batching windows; under mixed request-size load this caused head-of-line blocking and queue backlog, inflating tail latency and error rate. No model or code regression detected.
- Mitigation: engineering initiated rollback and reduced batching window; partial rollout shows ~35% improvement in p95 and reduced 504s. Full rollback ETA: 45–60 minutes from Dylan's 12:07 note on 02/19; complete by 13:15 PST on 02/19 (patchedd across pools).
- Customer impact: production user-facing failures for a subset of high-value requests; Stellarnet requests account for ~2% of their nightly traffic but represent high-value launch flows. Customer requested credits.

Ask for execs:
1) Approve offering a one-off credit of up to 10% of February invoice to maintain goodwill (we estimate $6k–$9k based on usage).
2) Approve priority postmortem and a resource allocation: 2 SRE engineers for 5 days to implement adaptive queue_depth autoscaling and a QA canary to prevent config rollouts from defaulting to higher latency-tuned settings.

I'll coordinate the customer-facing postmortem and timeline once you approve credits and the headcount request.

Attachments: incident_runbook_v2.pdf, trace-20260219.log, p95_spike_screenshot.png

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
